agent: game options wave, reader C (the Audio and Controls tabs, and the writer of settings.txt)
question: The in-game settings window's Audio and Controls tabs whole (mastervolume_slider, effectvolume_slider, musicvolume_slider, scrollspeed_slider, zoomspeed_slider, legacy_camera_checkbox: range, step, the setting each holds, at once or on Apply), and the writer of settings.txt: where and when it is written, every key in its order and format, which field of the settings object each is.

addresses.name: CSettingsScreen::InitAudioTab
addresses.comment: **The Audio tab's set-up**: finds `mastervolume_slider`, `effectvolume_slider` and `musicvolume_slider` in `menu_settings_AUDIO` (the window +0x368's slot 27 for the subwindow, then the subwindow's slot 19 for a scrollbar) and keeps them at +0x348, +0x34C and +0x350. **It attaches no observer to any of them** - unlike the Video tab's set-up (0x6F6E00), which attaches observers to its controls (trees_checkbox and gamma_slider at least, 0x6F6ECC and 0x6F6F77) - so a slider's move does nothing by itself: CSettingsScreen::UpdateVolumes (slot 4) copies the three positions into the settings every frame the window is up, which is what makes a volume heard as it moves. Called once, from CSettingsScreen::CSettingsScreen. 0x6F6AB0..0x6F6C98, bare `ret`; it abuts CSettingsScreen::InitGameTab, whose `ret` is the byte before it with no padding (trap 2). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.1.
addresses.evidence: Read whole: three `push <name>; push 'menu_settings_AUDIO'`, `call [[+0x368]+0x6C]`, `call [[eax]+0x4C]`, and the stores `mov [esi+0x348],eax` 0x6F6B30, `[esi+0x34C]` 0x6F6BC3, `[esi+0x350]` 0x6F6C52. The three names have one reference each in the image (0x6F6ADA, 0x6F6B69, 0x6F6BFC), all here. No call through the slider's +0x48 slot 1 (the add-observer the Video set-up makes at 0x6F6ECC) anywhere in the body. Wrong if another function attaches observers to +0x348..+0x350: a displacement scan of 0x6F2860..0x6FC000 finds them read only in UpdateVolumes, StoreChoices and CSettingsScreen_Refresh.

addresses.name: CSettingsScreen::InitControlsTab
addresses.comment: **The Controls tab's set-up**: finds `scrollspeed_slider` and `zoomspeed_slider` in `menu_settings_CONTROLS` and keeps them at +0x35C and +0x364. Like the Audio tab's, it attaches no observer. **`legacy_camera_checkbox` is not looked up here, nor anywhere but CSettingsScreen::StoreChoices** (its one reference, VA 0x6F8442), so the checkbox is never set from the settings: it shows the .gui's default, unticked, until the player ticks it, and Apply writes whatever it shows into use_legacy_camera. The two sliders' positions reach the settings only on Apply (StoreChoices), scroll speed raised to 5 and zoom speed to 1 where below. Called once, from CSettingsScreen::CSettingsScreen. 0x6F6CA0..0x6F6DF5, bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.2.
addresses.evidence: Read whole: two lookups (window slot 27 'menu_settings_CONTROLS', subwindow slot 19), stores `mov [esi+0x35C],eax` 0x6F6D20 and `mov [esi+0x364],eax` 0x6F6DAF. The string 'legacy_camera_checkbox' (VA 0x15D4A40) has exactly one reference in every section of the image, 0x6F8442, inside StoreChoices; positive control - 'counters_checkbox' has two, the second being CSettingsScreen_Refresh setting the box from the settings' +0xF9 at 0x6F9EDE..0x6F9F47. Wrong if the checkbox is reached by some route other than its name - a census of window-code reads of the settings' +0x188 finds none.

addresses.name: CSystemSettings_SaveToFile
addresses.comment: **Writes settings.txt.** Opens the file named by the settings' +0xC0 (`settings.txt`, or the name main.cpp loaded the settings from) through VirtualFile_Open for writing, text, mode empty - so PHYSFS_openWrite under PhysFS's write directory, truncating: `Documents\Paradox Interactive\Hearts of Iron III\settings.txt`, and with a mod the mod's own user folder (the maintainer's disk has a `BlackICE GitHub\settings.txt` beside the base one, both written by the game). Builds a CSaveWriter (VA table 0x15FD940, depth 0, binary = the file's +0x13) and calls **the settings' slot 2, SaveContents - not slot 1**, so the top level has no braces; then the writer and the file are destroyed, closing it. A file that will not open throws out of VirtualFile_Open (CSettingsScreen::OnApply calls this inside a try). Five callers: CSettingsScreen::OnApply (0x6F760F), **CInGameIdler::~CInGameIdler** (0x649789, so every time a game is left), COutLiner::OnConfigurationClose (0x6A7DA8), the multiplayer lobby's CONNECTED handler at VA 0x708190 (0x708548, after copying the player name into lastplayer and, in one mode, the host into lasthost) and the login dialog's handler at VA 0x7CC280 (0x7CC452, after copying the login name into lastplayer). Nothing writes it when the process quits from the main menu. 0xAB1CE0..0xAB1DDB, bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.4.
addresses.evidence: Read whole. `lea eax,[esi+0xC0]; push eax; ... lea ecx,[ebx+1]; call 0xA6C1B0` (VirtualFile_Open, text 1, write 1, mode ''), `mov edx,[esi]; call [edx+8]` with the writer at 0xAB1D6F. Every one of the five callers loads ESI from GetGameSettings or g_GameSettings just before the call (0x649787, 0x6A7DA6, 0x6F75E2/0x6F7605, 0x708546, 0x7CC450). findRefs --callers 0xAB1CE0 gives exactly five. Wrong if a sixth route calls CSettings slot 2 with a file writer: none was looked for beyond the direct calls.

addresses.name: CSystemSettings::SaveContents
addresses.comment: **The first half of settings.txt**, in this order: `gui` = { the block at +0x64 (GuiSettings_SaveContents) }, `graphics` = { the block at +8 (GraphicsSettings_SaveContents) }, then ten floats each written `%f` (six decimals, e.g. `55.000000`) as a tok_fixed-typed CToken: `sound_fx_volume` +0x84, `music_volume` +0x88, `scroll_speed` +0x90, `camera_rotation_speed` +0x94, `zoom_speed` +0x98, `mouse_speed` +0x9C, `master_volume` +0x80, `ambient_volume` +0x8C - and then `pause_on_event=no` **only when +0xA1 is clear**, nothing when it is set (the default). Slot 2 of the table 0x1600CFC (VA) the CSystemSettings constructor writes, which RTTI does not list; CSettings::SaveContents calls it first. `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.4.
addresses.evidence: Read whole: SaveWriteKey with ECX 0xBD (gui), 0xBE (graphics), 0x10E, 0x10F, 0x110, 0x111, 0x112, 0x113, 0x114, 0x169 in that order, each float `movss xmm0,[edi+N]`, cvtps2pd, sprintf with '%f' (VA 0x15FD134), CToken type 0xD, SaveWriteValue, SaveWriteToken(0x10); 0xAB1CBF `cmp byte [edi+0xA1],0; jne` around SaveWriteBool(0x1A5, 0). Token names from ghidra/saveTokens.json. The maintainer's settings.txt has exactly these ten keys in this order, with six decimals, and no pause_on_event.

addresses.name: CSystemSettings::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CSystemSettings::LoadKey(CSystemSettings* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: The base half of the settings file's reader, reached from CSettings::LoadKey's default case. **The keys its switch names**, 11 of them: `gui` (the block at +0x64, its slot 3), `graphics` (the block at +8, its slot 3), `sound_fx_volume` +0x84, `music_volume` +0x88, `scroll_speed` +0x90, `camera_rotation_speed` +0x94, `zoom_speed` +0x98, `mouse_speed` +0x9C, `master_volume` +0x80, `ambient_volume` +0x8C, each read by the float parser 0xA7B640, and `pause_on_event` +0xA1 by ParseBool. No clamp on any value read. Anything else is dropped in silence. Slot 4 of the table 0x1600CFC (VA). `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.5.
addresses.evidence: The switch is `key - 0xBD`, a byte table at VA 0xAB18F0 (0xE9 entries) into eleven case addresses at VA 0xAB18C0, decoded entry by entry against saveTokens.json; each case is `lea eax,[ecx+N]; mov ecx,parse; call 0xA7B640` or the ParseBool / sub-object slot 3 call. Called from 0x4604C2 in CSettings::LoadKey's default. Wrong if the byte table was misread: the decode gives exactly the ten keys SaveContents writes plus pause_on_event.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::~CInGameIdler
addresses.comment: The in-game idler's destructor, called from its scalar deleting destructor (slot 0, VA 0x649680). It puts back its three tables (VA 0x15CEB54, 0x15CED14 at +0xB0, 0x15CED20 at +0xB4), tears down what +0x1DE4 holds (VA 0x649D80), and **then writes settings.txt** (CSystemSettings_SaveToFile at 0x649789) - so the player's settings, the outliner's state among them, are saved every time a game is left. Only the opening was read. 0x6496E0..0x649D7F, bare `ret`, with VA 0x649D80 abutting it with no padding (trap 2). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.4.

addresses.name: CSettings::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CSettings::LoadKey(CSettings* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: The player's settings as the game writes them back. **The keys its switch names**, 10 of them, one case each: `autosave`, `categories`, `debug_saves`, `lasthost`, `lastplayer`, `mapRenderingOptions`, `outliner`, `serveradress`, `simple`, `use_legacy_camera`. Read from the switch by reversing/scripts/definitions.py. A loader may resolve further keys as names out of a database - CGovernment and CMinister both do - but anything that is neither is dropped in silence. **Its default case hands the key to CSystemSettings::LoadKey** (0x4604C2), which reads eleven more - `gui`, `graphics`, the eight floats (`sound_fx_volume`, `music_volume`, `scroll_speed`, `camera_rotation_speed`, `zoom_speed`, `mouse_speed`, `master_volume`, `ambient_volume`) and `pause_on_event` - so the file's keys are 21 in all. Where each lands: mapRenderingOptions the object at +0xDC (its slot 3), lastplayer +0x104, lasthost +0x120, serveradress +0x13C (a value of `localhost` is refused and the old one kept, inferred from the compare at 0x4602B7), debug_saves +0x158, autosave +0x15C (AutosaveFrequency_FromString; an empty value leaves it), simple +0x174, use_legacy_camera +0x188, categories the int vector at +0x178 (0x44B450), outliner the CList at +0x164 (emptied first). Written back by CSettings::SaveContents. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.5.

Read 0x4601D0..0x4604F9: the jump table at VA 0x4604FC/0x460514 for key-0x1CC (cases 0, 7, 8, 9, 12), the compares for 0x3E0, 0x444, 0x712, 0x7B7, 0x7BC, and the default `push eax; push parse; mov ecx,esi; call 0xAB17D0` at 0x4604BB. addresses.name: UpdateMapCamera
addresses.no_signature: Four stack arguments - it ends `ret 0x10` - **and** two objects in registers: the camera arrives in ESI and the mouse in EDI, both read before the prologue has finished. Under custom storage every parameter has to be placed or none does, and two of the four stack arguments have not been identified, so placing the rest would be a guess dressed as a fact. The fourth, at [ebp+0x14], is a float the zoom and scroll steps cap at 0.2 - inferred to be the frame's seconds.
addresses.comment:
**Moves the map camera, once a frame.** ESI is the camera (a MapCamera, which lives at CInGameIdler +0x1938), EDI the object the mouse position is asked of, and the first stack argument the one key states are asked of.

In order: dragging with the middle button, which works through the map projection rather than the screen; the arrow keys, tested as VK_LEFT, VK_UP, VK_RIGHT and VK_DOWN through the key object's +0x24; **the four screen edge tests at 0x23CE97** (see MapEdgeScrollTests); then clamping the result to the camera's limits.

**The settings it reads** (read 2026-11-04): a zoom step of height / 60 x 0.8 x zoom_speed / 100 (settings +0x98), which a turn of the wheel ([EDI] slot 21) takes x 20 x 0.75 off the wanted height (+0x344, down to +0x34C) or adds x 20 x 1.5 to it (up to +0x350) - so a notch out is twice a notch in; a scroll step of min(t, 0.2) x scroll_speed / 100 (+0x90) x 12 x height / 40, t the fourth stack argument; and **use_legacy_camera (+0x188) in three places**: unset, a wheel zoom that changes the height also pulls the look point (+0x334/+0x338) toward the map point under the mouse, by 1 - zoomstep x 20 / height of the distance, where the mouse is more than 6 pixels inside the view; and the camera's position (+0x33C/+0x340) and height (+0x348) each close 0.197 of the way to their targets a frame. Set, the zoom is straight down at the centre and both jump to their targets at once.

The rotation arithmetic has not been followed. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.3.
addresses.evidence: Revision adds the settings' reads to the comment and one sentence to no_signature. 0x63C6F9..0x63C747 (height, /60.0 at VA 0x160A4A8, x0.8 at 0x160A3E0, x[settings+0x98]/100), 0x63C74D..0x63C7BD ([ebp+0x14] capped by 0.2 at 0x160A260/0x171618C, x[+0x90]/100, x12 at 0x160AA48, xheight, /40 at 0x160A2F8), 0x63C7F9..0x63C8AE (x20 at 0x160A318, x0.75 at 0x160A638, x1.5 at 0x160A6B8, the clamps to +0x34C/+0x350), the three `cmp byte [eax+0x188],0` at 0x63C8BB (jne past the pull-to-mouse block 0x63C8C8..0x63CB3B), 0x63D066 (copies +0x334/+0x338 to +0x33C/+0x340) and 0x63D281 (copies +0x344 to +0x348), the easing factor 0.197 the double at VA 0x160AA40. Which wheel sign is which direction is read off the clamps: the subtracting branch is held at the minimum.

addresses.name: CEU3Application::Run
addresses.signature: void __fastcall CEU3Application::Run(CEU3Application* this@EDI, int unknown1@stack:4, int unknown2@stack:8)
addresses.comment: The run loop main.cpp:601 calls. Takes the application in EDI and never writes edi - trap 11 again. Pins the process to one CPU through GetProcessAffinityMask/SetThreadAffinityMask, calls vftable slot 7 (which for CEU3Application is the shared empty stub 0xABF890, so nothing), then loops 0xA910A1..0xA9142D until this->+0xF8 == 0x12. Per frame it calls slot 1 of the current screen at 0xA9138D; the pending-screen swap at 0xA913A0 runs only when this->+0x88 is set, and that block calls the incoming screen's slot 2, then SLOT 3 at 0xA9140C, then slot 5. That is how CFrontEnd slot 3 (0x6EEF00) is reached, and it is why slot 3 is a one-shot activation hook rather than per-frame work. Signature corrected 2026-10-02 by the signature audit (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-sigaudit.md). **Each frame it also applies the settings' sound** (read 2026-11-04, through this->+0xEC, the settings): effects at master_volume / 100 x sound_fx_volume / 100 to the sound object (the singleton at VA 0x1B167C4, a CNullSound until a device replaces it; its slot 20) and music at master_volume / 100 x music_volume / 100 to the music object (VA 0x1B16808, a CNullMusic until replaced; its slot 7), each only when it differs from the last value sent (VA 0x174C4B8, 0x174C4B4); and mouse_speed as (int)(mouse_speed / 100 x 4 + 1) to this->+0xE4's slot 9. So a volume moved in the settings window is heard the frame after. ambient_volume and camera_rotation_speed are not read here. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.1.
addresses.evidence: Revision adds the sound paragraph only. 0xA91113..0xA9128A: `mov eax,[edi+0xEC]`, the products with 0.01 (VA 0x160A288) of +0x80 x +0x88 and +0x80 x +0x84, ucomisd against the two cached globals, `call [[0x1B167C4]+0x50]` and the music object's `call [[0x1B16808]+0x1C]`; 0xA91352..0xA9138B for +0x9C x 0.01 x 4.0 + 1.0, cvttsd2si, `call [[edi+0xE4]+0x24]`. That +0xEC is the settings is by layout - the same four offsets, and CEU3Application::LoadEverything does the same sums through it at startup (0x630C9D) - not by finding the store: inferred. The singletons' default classes from their constructors' tables (0x15CD1E4 CNullSound, 0x15CD25C CNullMusic).

struct_fields.name: language
struct_fields.comment: The gui block's `language` (the block sits at +0x64; this is its +8): 1 l_english (the constructor's), 2 l_french, 3 l_german, 4 l_polish, 5 l_spanish, 6 l_italian, 7 l_swedish, 8 l_czech, 9 l_hungarian, 10 l_dutch, 11 l_portugese, 12 l_russian, 13 l_finnish. The first of the sixteen bytes GameSettings_GetTextColours copies (+0x6C..+0x7B), so CInternationalizedText::Render is handed the language - the record's 'text colours' reading of those bytes is suspect. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.4.
struct_fields.evidence: GuiSettings_SaveContents switches on [gui+8] over 13 language tokens; its loader (VA 0xB41EA8) writes [ecx+8] from the l_* token; CSystemSettings::CSystemSettings writes [esi+0x6C] = 1 beside the gui table at +0x64.

struct_fields.name: has_set_language
struct_fields.comment: The gui block's `has_set_language` (its +0x18): written `yes` only where set. What sets it in play was not read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.4.
struct_fields.evidence: GuiSettings_SaveContents 0xB42176 `movzx eax,[edi+0x18]; test; je` around SaveWriteBool(0x1A3 has_set_language); the loader's case 0x1A3 is ParseBool into ecx+0x18.

struct_fields.name: master_volume
struct_fields.comment: `master_volume`, 0..100 from the window's mastervolume_slider, 100 from the constructor. Scales both effects and music (CEU3Application::Run, each frame); at 0 or below the front end and in-game music starts are skipped (0x60B9AC, 0x630DDD, 0x654046, 0x6EDE6D compare it with 0.0); **below -0.01 the settings window greys all three volume sliders** (CSettingsScreen_Refresh, 0x6FA356). Written into the file ninth, `%f`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.1.
struct_fields.evidence: Writers: CSettingsScreen::UpdateVolumes 0x6F6899, StoreChoices 0x6F82A6, the two Close bodies 0x6FB645/0x6FB8EE, the constructor and slot 6; read by CSystemSettings::LoadKey (case 0x114) and written by CSystemSettings::SaveContents (0xAB1C19). The -0.01 is the float at VA 0x160A518.

struct_fields.name: sound_fx_volume
struct_fields.comment: `sound_fx_volume`, 0..100 from effectvolume_slider, 100 from the constructor; the sound effects play at master/100 x this/100 (CEU3Application::Run). Written first of the eight floats. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.1.
struct_fields.evidence: UpdateVolumes 0x6F68BB from the slider at +0x34C; CSystemSettings::SaveContents 0xAB1A22 under key 0x10E; Run 0xA91157.

struct_fields.name: music_volume
struct_fields.comment: `music_volume`, 0..100 from musicvolume_slider, 100 from the constructor; the music plays at master/100 x this/100. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.1.
struct_fields.evidence: UpdateVolumes 0x6F68D7 from the slider at +0x350; SaveContents 0xAB1A7A under key 0x10F; Run 0xA91129.

struct_fields.name: ambient_volume
struct_fields.comment: `ambient_volume`, 50 from the constructor. No control in the settings window, and no reader was found outside the settings' own load and save. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.5.
struct_fields.evidence: Key 0x169 in CSystemSettings::LoadKey and SaveContents (0xAB1C6C). A scan for +0x8C within 40 instructions of every fetch of the settings (GetGameSettings, g_GameSettings, CEU3Application +0xEC) found no float read; the same scan finds +0x80's four readers.

struct_fields.name: camera_rotation_speed
struct_fields.comment: `camera_rotation_speed`, 50 from the constructor. No control in the window, and no reader found outside the load and save (the same scan as ambient_volume). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.5.
struct_fields.evidence: Key 0x111 in CSystemSettings::LoadKey and SaveContents (0xAB1B20); the fetch-site scan found no read.

struct_fields.name: mouse_speed
struct_fields.comment: `mouse_speed`, 50 from the constructor. No control in the window; CEU3Application::Run hands (int)(it / 100 x 4 + 1) to the application's +0xE4 slot 9 each frame. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.5.
struct_fields.evidence: Key 0x113 in LoadKey and SaveContents (0xAB1BC6); Run 0xA91352..0xA9138B.

struct_fields.name: pause_on_event
struct_fields.comment: `pause_on_event`, 1 from the constructor. The writer puts `pause_on_event=no` in the file only when it is clear and nothing when it is set, so the key is absent from a file in the default state. Readers outside the load and save were not looked for. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.4.
struct_fields.evidence: CSystemSettings::SaveContents 0xAB1CBF `cmp byte [edi+0xA1],0; jne` past SaveWriteBool(0x1A5, 0); LoadKey case 0x1A5 ParseBool into +0xA1; constructor and slot 6 `mov byte [..+0xA1],1`.

struct_fields.name: file_name
struct_fields.comment: The name settings.txt is read from and written to: `settings.txt` from the constructor; main.cpp's load (VA 0xAB1E80, called at 0xA58E7C) assigns the name it is given - `settings.txt`, or a string main holds when it is not empty (inferred to come from the command line, not traced). CSystemSettings_SaveToFile opens it under PhysFS's write directory. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.4.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor 0xAB1716..0xAB172F assigns 'settings.txt' (VA 0x15FC1FC) at esi+0xC0; 0xAB1EB0 `lea ecx,[esi+0xC0]; call 0x401BD0` from the argument; 0xAB1D23 `lea eax,[esi+0xC0]` into VirtualFile_Open. main's choice at 0xA58E3A..0xA58E69 tests the length of a local at [ebp-0x218].

struct_fields.name: categories
struct_fields.comment: The file's `categories = { ... }`, a vector of ints: six zeros from the constructor, read by 0x44B450, written space-separated by 0x4608D0 (not at all when empty). struct_fields.name: use_legacy_camera
struct_fields.comment: `use_legacy_camera`, no from the constructor. Set: UpdateMapCamera zooms at the screen's centre and moves the camera and its height to their targets at once; clear: the zoom pulls toward the mouse and both ease 0.197 of the way a frame. **Written only by the settings window's Apply, from legacy_camera_checkbox, which nothing sets from this field** - so Apply with the box as the .gui leaves it turns it off. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-settingswindow.md, section C.3.
struct_fields.evidence: StoreChoices 0x6F849A..0x6F84F5 (`cmp [box+0x60],1; sete` then +0x188); readers 0x63C8BB, 0x63D066, 0x63D281 in UpdateMapCamera; SaveContents 0x4606A2 under 0x7BC; LoadKey case 0x7BC ParseBool. The census of reads of +0x188 near every settings fetch gives those three and no other.

slots_noted: CSystemSettings' own table (VA 0x1600CFC: slot 0 0xAB17A0, 2 SaveContents 0xAB19E0, 4 LoadKey 0xAB17D0) and the graphics and gui blocks' tables (VA 0x1600624, 0x16078F8) are not RTTI tables, so their functions are named by convention without vftable_slots records. CInGameIdler slot 0 (0x649680, the scalar deleting destructor) is not recorded.
